$schema.description: The JSON Schema this config is written against. ocel init writes the schema shipped with the CLI that created it.

allowDegraded.description: The needs this project waives rather than have a deploy refused over.

apps.description: The apps this project deploys. Left off, ocel detects one at the project root.

arch.description: The processor architecture an app's functions or container image are built for. Left off, what the provider runs the app on.

build.description: How a container app's image is built.

command.description: The command that builds the app inside the image. Left off, the app's own build script runs.

context.description: The directory the image is built from, relative to the project. Left off, it is the workspace root the app belongs to.

dockerfile.description: The Dockerfile to build from. A relative path resolves against the app's directory.

build.title: BuildConfig

compute.description: What the app runs on: serverless functions packed per route, or one container image serving everything.

domains.description: The hostnames this app is served on.

production.description: The hostnames production is served on.

domains.title: AppDomainConfig

entrypoint.description: The file the app is served from, when it is not the one ocel would detect.

folder.description: The variables folder this app reads, when it does not read the project's own.

framework.description: What a serverless app is built with, when ocel is not to read it off the app's own manifest.

health.description: How a container app is checked before it is served.

path.description: The path the check requests, off the app's own root. Any 2xx answer means up. Left off, the check requests /.

health.title: HealthConfig

name.description: The app's name. It is a label of every resource the app deploys and of its preview hostname, so it is a DNS label.

path.description: The app's directory, relative to the config.

bindings.description: Resources this project declares that ocel binds instead of provisioning them itself. Keyed by resource type, then by the name the app declares. The value is "@" followed by the name a record your own infrastructure published, such as "@warehouse", and a name nothing has published refuses the deploy; or the record written inline, checked at deploy rather than provisioned, optionally keyed by the tier it serves.

discovery.description: Where the resources an app declares are found.

paths.description: The directories holding infrastructure declarations, relative to the config. Left off, ocel reads the default discovery directory.

discovery.title: DiscoveryConfig

dns.description: Where the project's hostname records are written, keyed by the DNS service's identifier and holding its options, or named alone.

zone.description: The zone the records are written into. Omit it and ocel picks the zone that covers the hostname.
The zone the records are written into. Omit it and ocel picks the zone that covers the hostname.

dns.title: DnsDescriptor

domains.description: The hostnames this project is served on.

preview.description: The wildcard hostname previews are served under, such as *.preview.example.com.

production.description: The hostnames production is served on.

domains.title: ProjectDomainConfig

edge.description: The edge in front of the origin, keyed by its identifier and holding its options, or named alone. Omit it and the provider fronts the deployment with its own default edge.
edge.title: EdgeDescriptor

provider.description: The provider ocel deploy provisions into, keyed by its identifier and holding its options. A provider that needs no options may be named alone.

certificates.description: Certificates to serve a hostname with, keyed by hostname, valued by the ARN of an already-issued ACM certificate. A hostname left off gets a certificate ocel requests, validates and deletes again.

region.description: The AWS region to deploy into.

varsKey.description: ARN of a KMS key to encrypt this account's variables under. Omit it and ocel bootstrap --features vars-key makes a key ocel owns.

project.description: The Google Cloud project to deploy into.

region.description: The region to deploy into. A project spans them all, so this names the one.

certificates.description: Certificates to serve a hostname with, keyed by hostname, valued by the path to the certificate on the machine.

deployKey.description: Path to the public key the ocel-deploy login accepts; defaults to the bootstrapping login's keys.

proxy.description: What fronts this machine on ports 80 and 443. Leave it out and ocel runs its own proxy; name the one the machine already runs to deploy behind it.

traefik.description: A Traefik the machine already runs, reading ocel's routes from a directory its file provider watches.

directory.description: The directory Traefik's file provider watches, where ocel writes its routers.

entrypoints.description: The entry points ocel's routers attach to.

http.description: The entry point ocel's http-to-https redirect routers attach to; web when left out.

https.description: The entry point ocel's hostname routers attach to; websecure when left out.

entrypoints.title: VpsEntrypoints

network.description: A docker network ocel's switchboard joins, so Traefik reaches it by name. Not with port.

port.description: The loopback port ocel's switchboard is published on for Traefik to reach; 8480 when left out. Not with network.

preset.description: The host tool whose Traefik this is. It fills in every other field, and a field written beside it overrides.

previewResolver.description: A resolver that can issue the preview base's wildcard over DNS-01. Set, previews share one wildcard certificate; left out, each preview hostname gets its own from resolver.

resolver.description: The certificate resolver every hostname router ocel writes names.

directory.description: The directory Traefik's file provider watches, where ocel writes its routers.

entrypoints.description: The entry points ocel's routers attach to.

http.description: The entry point ocel's http-to-https redirect routers attach to; web when left out.

https.description: The entry point ocel's hostname routers attach to; websecure when left out.

entrypoints.title: VpsEntrypoints

network.description: A docker network ocel's switchboard joins, so Traefik reaches it by name. Not with port.

port.description: The loopback port ocel's switchboard is published on for Traefik to reach; 8480 when left out. Not with network.

previewResolver.description: A resolver that can issue the preview base's wildcard over DNS-01. Set, previews share one wildcard certificate; left out, each preview hostname gets its own from resolver.

resolver.description: The certificate resolver every hostname router ocel writes names.

traefik.title: VpsTraefik

caddy.description: A Caddy the machine already runs, importing ocel's site blocks from a directory.

config.description: The config file caddy reload names inside the container; /etc/caddy/Caddyfile when left out.

container.description: The container Caddy runs in; left out, Caddy runs as the systemd caddy.service.

directory.description: The directory the running Caddy imports site blocks from.

network.description: A docker network ocel's switchboard joins, so Caddy reaches it by name. Not with port.

port.description: The loopback port ocel's switchboard is published on for Caddy to reach; 8480 when left out. Not with network.

preset.description: The host tool whose Caddy this is. It fills in every other field, and a field written beside it overrides.

config.description: The config file caddy reload names inside the container; /etc/caddy/Caddyfile when left out.

container.description: The container Caddy runs in; left out, Caddy runs as the systemd caddy.service.

directory.description: The directory the running Caddy imports site blocks from.

network.description: A docker network ocel's switchboard joins, so Caddy reaches it by name. Not with port.

port.description: The loopback port ocel's switchboard is published on for Caddy to reach; 8480 when left out. Not with network.

caddy.title: VpsCaddy

manual.description: A proxy you route to ocel yourself; ocel writes nothing to it.

network.description: A docker network ocel's switchboard also joins, so a proxy on it reaches the switchboard by name even after it is recreated.

port.description: The loopback port your proxy forwards to ocel's switchboard on; 8480 when left out.

manual.title: VpsManual

proxy.title: VpsProxy

ssh.description: The machine to deploy onto: a Host alias from ssh_config, or the destination spelled out.

host.description: The hostname or address to reach the machine at.

identityFile.description: The private key to authenticate with, as a path.

port.description: The port sshd listens on. Omit it and ssh's own default stands.

user.description: The account to log in as. Omit it and ssh resolves the user itself.

provider.title: ProviderDescriptor

registry.description: Where this project's container images are pushed.

password.description: The environment variable holding the password or token, written as "${REGISTRY_TOKEN}" and read where the push authenticates — never the secret itself.

server.description: The registry host and the namespace images sit under, such as ghcr.io/acme. No scheme, and no credentials.

username.description: The username the push authenticates as, where the registry wants one.

registry.title: RegistryConfig

slug.description: The project's deployment identity. Every stack and resource ocel creates in your own account is keyed on it, so changing it forks a new project.

transforms.description: Transform modules applied while provisioning, in order — later modules win where their patches collide. Each is a path to a module whose default export is a defineTransform(...) result, keyed by the provider it patches.
